policydecision_details: Announced that from July 1, 2026, franchise AP holders may import only completely built‑up (CBU) electric vehicles, aiming to encourage greater localisation in mass‑market segments.
Issued the Decree 161/2026/ND-CP base salary and bonus regime for cadres, civil servants, public employees, armed forces. From July 01, 2026, the base salary is VND 2,530,000/month (usd100).

The first Vietnam Grand Sale in 2026 will take place from July 1-31 nationwide. The annual event is expected to attract broad participation from businesses across sectors through traditional trade promotion activities and e-commerce initiatives.

The United States and Iran have reached a peace agreement to implement an immediate and permanent cessation of military operations. As part of this deal, the United States will remove its naval blockade of Iranian ports and reopen the Strait of Hormuz to international shipping to facilitate the flow of energy and essential commodities like fertilizer.
contextoradditionalinfo: The blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, a vital route for global energy supplies, caused significant economic disruption, including inflated energy prices and supply chain congestion for essential agricultural inputs like fertilizer, threatening global food production.

policydecision_details: Doubled the child nutrition allowance for Dalit children under five to Rs1,000 per month (about USD 7.5), increasing the programme allocation from Rs2.08 billion (around USD 16 million) to Rs3 billion (about USD 23 million).
Unveiled incentives, including grants of up to 40% for about 20 million in agriculture and livestock production, to boost productivity and make farming more profitable and attractive.

The Health Promotion Board will conduct regular checks to ensure accurate labeling. It requests the beverages such as coconut water that exceed sugar content thresholds must display Nutri-Grade labels rated “C” or “D,” with non-compliance constituting an offence.
Raised the small business tax transition threshold to 5 billion soums (about USD 400,000) to curb revenue misreporting and support enterprise growth.

Offered youth concessional loans of up to 100 million soums (about USD 8,000) under the “Youth Business” programme to support entrepreneurship and employment, with extended repayment and grace periods, one year for principal payments and up to three months for interest payments .
Considered tax cuts and subsidies to boost electric vehicle uptake, including incentives of up to 70,000 baht (about USD 2,145) for up to 150,000 vehicles, depending on type and model.
The programme has spent about 1,084 million baht, with 5 million users participating across over 566,000 shops, out of more than 26 million approved beneficiaries.

Unveiled a new stimulus package for the second half of 2026 to boost consumer spending and support labor markets. Announced by Coordinating Minister for Economic Affairs, the package includes tax cuts aligned with President campaign pledge.

The French government has announced a mid-year increase in the national minimum wage (SMIC), boosting it by 2.41 percent in response to persistent inflationary pressures. The new rate takes effect on June 1, 2026, and will automatically raise salary thresholds for several key immigration and work visa categories.

policy_description: Subsidies on fuel, power and water
policydecision_details: Sri Lanka’s fuel subsidy allocation of Rs57 billion (USD 195 million) will end by June, even as prices remain below cost, with temporary accommodation by the IMF.
policycategory: Subsidies on fuel, power and water

policydecision_details: Planned to tighten fuel quotas as the CPC’s import bill reached USD 524 million in May, reflecting rising foreign exchange pressures amid efforts to curb fuel consumption during the ongoing economic crisis.

Introduced a new prudential levy on banks, insurers, and other financial institutions, shifting the cost of regulation to the financial industry and aligning with the funding approach of the Financial Markets Authority and the Commerce Commission.
Enacted the revised expatriate salary policy.

policy_description: Unspecified production support|Ecosystem and habitat preservation
policydecision_details: Launched a national programme through 2030 to support sustainable business practices, targeting 25,000 enterprises and the development of at least 20 scalable pilot models.
policycategory: Unspecified production support|Ecosystem and habitat preservation

policydecision_details: Enforced stricter food safety rules for kindergartens, including bans on high-risk foods, tighter limits on additives, and requirements that suppliers have no food safety violations in the past three year
Planned “one-gate” export system, centralized under Danantara Sumberdaya Indonesia (DSI), is raising monopoly concerns.

Enacted the “Administrative Measures for the Registration of Overseas Food Production Enterprises Importing Food into China” (GACC Decree No. 280), issued on 14 October 2025. The new regulations require all foreign food exporters to comply with updated procedures, although most businesses are already largely compliant. The measures aim to strengthen the safety of imported food and support the long-term sustainability of international food trade.

Opened the registration for the “Thais Help Thais Plus” programme to up to 30 million people, offering a 60/40 co-payment scheme in which the government subsidizes 60% of eligible spending. The support covers food, beverages, goods, and selected services purchased from participating businesses.

More protection for bees and other pollinators, such as wasps and butterflies, and the planting of new trees. These are two of the innovations provided for in Legislative Decree 80/2026, in force since 31 May 2026, for the protection of nature, which adapts national legislation to the provisions of EU Regulation 2024/1991.

Bangladesh–US Cotton Trade Agreement is under negotiation. The US cotton initiative identifies Bangladesh as a key market, with plans to boost American cotton exports. Bangladesh may benefit from tariff reductions on apparel made with US cotton and textile inputs, along with additional trade concessions.
decision_making_institution: Government of United States of America

policy_description: Subsidies on fuel, power and water
policydecision_details: Extended measures aimed at limiting fuel price increase for an additional two months. For diesel, the government will maintain a subsidy of 1.12 reais (USD 0.22) per liter for domestic refiners and fuel importers beginning June 1. Officials said two subsidy programs introduced in April will be merged into a single mechanism intended to support price stability.
policycategory: Subsidies on fuel, power and water

policydecision_details: Banned single-use plastic water bottles in state institutions, directing government agencies to stop their use and take immediate steps to eliminate single-use plastics.
Planned to introduce a “Blue Lane” customs clearance system for authorized businesses to streamline trade and expedite processing.
Japan is preparing a supplementary budget of about ¥3 trillion (around $19 billion) to ease living costs amid high energy prices and a weak yen, while keeping 2026 bond issuance unchanged.

Committed USD 3.8 billion to nature as critical infrastructure: The government’s new strategy, A Force of Nature, aims to restore habitats, align industrial and conservation efforts, and mobilize investment for nature protection. Expected outcomes of Canada’s A Force of Nature strategy include: Restored ecosystems and critical habitats, improving biodiversity and resilience Better alignment of industrial activity with conservation goals, reducing environmental impacts Increased public and private investment in nature, including new financing mechanisms Enhanced climate resilience, such as carbon sequestration and natural disaster mitigation Stronger protection of natural areas, contributing to national and global conservation targets
Gazzetted the Water Skiing and Motor Boat control Bill 2026, containing amendments on the application areas and on the speed limits.
Gazzetted the Value Added Tax 2026, contains amendments on the application of VAT.

Classified 14 minerals as critical, banning the export of all raw or unbeneficiated forms, and mandated state shareholding through special-purpose vehicles, a long-awaited codification of industrial policy that follows a dramatic surge in lithium revenue.
Unveiled reforms to modernize its capital market, including introducing intraday trading, with the aim of creating a more dynamic, technology-driven, and globally competitive financial system.
Japan’s parliament has passed a bill to strengthen oversight of foreign investments, with the upper house approving revisions to the Foreign Exchange and Foreign Trade Act.

Expanded monitoring requirements to includ plastic containers , glass bottles, aluminium casks, and papaer cartons used in food and beverages packaging. Specific tariff codes (es. 3915.10.00.00, 3923.30.91.00, 4811.59.20.00) are now clearly defined to ensure stricter control and compliance. This update reflects a broader effort to modernize sanitary surveillance and strengthen food safety standards across all packaging materials in commercial distribution.

Distributed over 1.9 million bags of fertilizers to nearly one million farmers, as a part of efforts to boost agricultural productivity and strengthen food security nationwide. Fertiliser distribution was complemented by 12,000 litres of organic fertiliser, while 109 fertiliser inspectors and 329 industry stakeholders were trained on regulatory compliance to curb fake agricultural inputs.
Formalized preferential tariffs on selected Taiwanese exports, capping Section 232 tariffs at 15% for certain auto parts, timber, and wood products
decision_making_institution: Government of Taiwan Province of China

policydecision_details: Announced a series of trade defense measures, including actions aimed at the steel industry, as well as expanded support for exporters. The agency approved the inclusion of carbon steel bars on the list of products subject to temporary tariff increases due to temporary trade imbalances, raising the number of covered items to 20. The measure meets a request from Aço Brasil (IABr), which represents Brazil’s steelmakers.
Signed an agreement with Viet Nam have to commit the open and uninterrupted trade flows, ensuring the continued operation of key transport and trade infrastructure to minimize disruptions.

Nepal’s government has reduced the overall agricultural budget 2026/2027, despite increasing fertilizer allocations to Rs28.82 billion (about USD 215–220 million), while committing to introduce a fertilizer supply calendar.

policy_description: Agricultural expenditure in the national budget
policydecision_details: Nepal’s 2026–27 budget, presented on May 29 under Prime Minister Balendra Shah, comes at a critical economic turning point, with strong public expectations and a stable government. It allocates Rs3.63 billion to the labour sector, focusing on safer foreign employment, skills development, and measures such as zero-cost migration and remittance investment schemes.
policycategory: Agricultural expenditure in the national budget

policydecision_details: Kazakhstan and Russia have reached a financial agreement for a 2.4 GW nuclear power project, featuring two VVER‑1200 Generation III+ reactors and an estimated cost of about USD 16.5 billion. Major construction is expected to begin in 2027.

Launched a Greenhouse Crop Insurance product aimed at protecting farmers against losses and boosting investment in climate smart-agriculture. The insurance product was unveiled during an event held at the headquarters of the National Institute of Statistics of Rwanda (NISR), bringing together 123 farmers from all districts of the country, representatives from insurance companies, and senior officials from the Ministry of Agriculture and Animal Resources (MINAGRI), the Rwanda Agriculture and Animal Resources Development Board (RAB), and the National Agricultural Export Development Board (NAEB).

On May 4, 2026, the Netherlands issued Regulation of the Minister of Health, Welfare and Sport of April 23, 2026 (reference 4375777-1097324-WJZ), amending the requirements for food contact ceramics under the Commodities Act (Regulation on Packaging and Consumer Products) (‘the Regulation’). This revision is related to the Decision of the Benelux Committee of Ministers concerning ceramic articles intended to come into contact with food. The new law will become effective on May 29, 2026.

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: Launched a consultation on its Renewable Energy Strategy to 2035, targeting 22–26 GW of installed capacity and aiming for renewables to account for 35%–40% of the power mix.
policycategory: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policydecision_details: Poland has introduced a temporary ban on imports of fruits and vegetables containing traces of four pesticides prohibited in the EU, aiming to prompt action from the European Commission at the EU level.
Announced reformes against cattle rustling to protect small producers.

The USDA has announced over USD 9.75 million in funding through the Acer and Micro-Grants for Food Security programs to support the maple syrup industry and strengthen local food production in food-insecure communities. Eligible applicants are agricultural agencies, commissions, or departments in Alaska, American Samoa, the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands, the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, the Federated States of Micronesia, Guam, Hawaii, the Republic of the Marshall Islands, the Republic of Palau, and the United States Virgin Islands.
decision_making_institution: Government of United States of America

policy_description: Animal health measures|Livestock measures and regulations
policydecision_details: Adopted a joint 2026-2028 Action Plan with South Africa aimed at strengthen regional cooperation in the fight against Foot and Mouth Disease. The action plan includes coordinated vaccination campaigns, maintenance of border fences, strengthening of diagnostic capacity and joint livestock farmer training programmes in key border regions such as Lobatse-Mahikeng and Francistown-Musina.
policycategory: Animal health measures|Livestock measures and regulations

policydecision_details: Confirmed that the New World screwworm is not present domestically but remains a growing threat, prompting livestock import restrictions from Mexico and heightened surveillance. Authorities have launched a multi‑agency response, including emergency drug authorizations and containment measures, to prevent outbreaks and limit potential economic losses exceeding USD 2 billion.
decision_making_institution: Government of United States of America

policydecision_details: Launched a reform of its forestry and water management service as it is grappling with mounting environmental and climate-related risks. The proposed legislation calls for a broad modernisation of the service aimed at improving its operational effectiveness, nationwide reach, and monitoring and response capabilities. The reform would also expand the service’s responsibilities in areas including sustainable forest resource management, protected area conservation, reforestation, law enforcement, and public awareness campaigns.

Piloted part-time employment system. The initiative has launched in Thimphu, attracting about 130 job seekers, with up to 50 companies set to participate under the Department of Employment and Entrepreneurship.

policy_description: Seed technology and quality assurance systems
policydecision_details: Announed two major strategic framrworks designed to transform its seed industru over the next five year (the National Seed Sector Development Plan, the National Seed System Investment Plan) both covering the period 2026-2030.
policycategory: Seed technology and quality assurance systems

policydecision_details: Enacted the Credit Reference Act 2025, aimed at strengthenining the country's financial system and improving access to credit. The Bill seeks to repeal and replace the Credit Reference Act of 2011. It provides a legal framework for the establishment and regulation of credit reference bureaus, sets conditions for credit reporting, and addresses other related financial matters.

Allowed microfinance institutions to offer factoring services, with a reform aiming to improve financing access for small businesses. Factoring allows a company to receive immediate cash by selling unpaid invoices to a financial institution.

policy_description: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures|Water policies and regulations
policydecision_details: Introduced a Senate bill to redefine Puerto Rico's Maritime-Terrestrial Zone to reflect sea-leve rise and other climate risks not addressed under current law, that defines the Maritime-Terrestrial Zone as the coastal area affected by tides and storm waves, including reclaimed lands and riverbanks up to navigable or tidal points. The bill argues that the existing framework no longer reflects Puerto Rico’s “present climate reality” because it does not adequately address rising sea levels, coastal erosion or the protection of coastal ecosystems and public access.
policycategory: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures|Water policies and regulations

policydecision_details: Signed into a law a measure that eliminates 6 percent tax previously levied on airlines tickets. The airline ticket tax reform signals a policy shift aimed at reducing operational costs for carriers and stimulating growth in the country's aviation industry. This move is expected to make Paraguay a more appealing destination for international airlines to establish and expand their services.
Approved a law that requires multination entities fomiciled in the country to demonstrate real local operations or face a 15 percent tax on passive foreign income.

policy_description: Unspecified production support|Public/mutual fund and contingent risk financing
policydecision_details: Announced a post-flood recovery plan worth around USD 120 million, at a time when the agricultural campaign faces major challenges in ensuring national food security. The objective is to assist affected families, restore productive areas and reduce the impact of losses already recorded.
policycategory: Unspecified production support|Public/mutual fund and contingent risk financing

policydecision_details: The Bank of Israel set the shekel at NIS 2.84 per dollar, up 0.665% from May 28, while it weakened 0.878% against sterling to NIS 3.817 per pound.

The Monetary Authority of Singapore’s (MAS) moved to remove mandatory financial advice for most investors signals a shift in approach, while keeping safeguards in place for vulnerable customers.
Urged the government to make timely arrangements to ensure that farmers do not face a shortage of fertilizer during the planting season this year.

Indian onion exports to the Maldives will continue under a quota system set through a trade agreement, similar to special arrangements India has made with several other partner countries as Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Mauritius, Bahrain, Bhutan and Nepal .

policy_description: Sanitary, phytosanitary and technical standards improvements
policydecision_details: Secured approval to export ten types of dried vegetables to China after meeting phytosanitary requirements, opening new market opportunities for its agricultural sector.
policycategory: Sanitary, phytosanitary and technical standards improvements

policydecision_details: Expanded agricultural drone use through learning centres and farmer training to cut costs, raise yields and build smart farming skills. AEROTHAI’s drone farming pilot in Nakhon Phanom shows strong gains: seed use fell 52%, fertiliser 25%, and labour costs 41%. Yields rose to 1,100 kg/rai (+250 kg), boosting net income to 5,254 baht/rai—about 2,509 baht higher than traditional methods.

Approved new open banking regulations to increase competition and innovation by requiring banks to securely share customer data with authorized third-party providers, with user consent. These rules strengthen data protection, promote transparency, and enable new digital financial services such as payment initiation and account aggregation.

The Ministry of Finance announced the launch of “Diaspora Invests at Home,” a new EUR 100 million (USD 116 million) program designed to support Romanians living abroad who want to start businesses and invest in Romania.
Lombardy imposes up to 200 percent tax penalties on rural data centers while competitors offer billion-dollar incentives.
The Minister for Social Protection launched the Roadmap for Social Inclusion 2026–2030 at the Department of Social Protection’s Social Inclusion Forum in the Aviva Stadium in Dublin.

The Czech government has approved a bill that would significantly tighten the conditions for Ukrainian refugees staying in the country, reflecting a broader European trend in which governments are gradually reducing benefits and tightening support systems that were introduced after the outbreak of the Russian-Ukrainian war in 2022.

The European Commission has approved the disbursement of the third tranche of funds under the EU Growth Plan for Montenegro in the total amount of EUR 44.2 million (USD 51.4 million), once again confirming the European Union’s confidence in Montenegro’s reform process and the results achieved on its European path.

Authorised a comprehensive new strategy for Santiago Island, introducing strict regulations for coastal and maritime activities to combact environmental degradation and climate risk. The Management Plan for the Coastal Zone and Adjacent Sea, published Tuesday in the Official Gazette and effective immediately, establishes a new legal framework for the nation’s most populous island. The policy addresses the unique challenges of an island nation where economic survival is inextricably linked to the coastline.
Adopted the budget for the fiscal year 2026/2027.

Unveiled its first open‑source agricultural AI model, Green Shield, a large language model designed to provide scientific farming guidance and support proper pesticide use for crop protection.

Updated master plans for 68 of its 79 cities as part of its urban development strategy, with the Baku Master Plan to 2040 highlighting its modern planning approach.

Bangladesh’s draft Import Policy 2026-2029 proposes increasing export value‑addition requirements, to promote local sourcing and reduce reliance on imports, though industry leaders warn the measures could hurt export competitiveness.

Launched a new offshore bidding round for 26 oil and gas blocks, offering revised production‑sharing terms, including export rights, tax incentives, and more flexible pricing, to attract investors after a failed 2024 round.

Sold subsidised meat for Eid al-Adha under blockade.

Bank of Thailand (BOT) outlined stricter regulations for three branchless banks in Thailand, aiming to promote savings, facilitate access to credit, and curb price-cutting strategies.

Removed OpenAI from its VAT collector list for digital services, as part of ongoing adjustments in April 2026. The update, issued by the Directorate General of Taxes, also includes new additions such as Hashi Corp., Inc. and Perplexity AI, Inc.

Planned to explore the creation of investment funds for individual investors to expand small‑scale investment opportunities, including developing new financial instruments and involving investment companies.

Approved a State Program for expanding financial inclusion in Azerbaijan for 2027–2030. The decree assigns the Central Bank responsibility for coordinating and monitoring implementation, while the Center for Analysis of Economic Reforms and Communication will evaluate progress.
Planned to exit its existing USD 5.5 billion IMF programme and negotiate a new 3-4 year arrangement worth USD 5-6 billion, aiming for more flexible reform conditions and continued financial support.
Provided AUD 10 million in grants to 49 organisations to support local jobs initiatives, helping more Australians move into secure work under the extended Local Jobs Programme.

Tightened scrutiny of land holdings linked to foreign nationals, targeting the use of nominee arrangements to bypass ownership laws. Inspection committees will be set up nationwide to strengthen enforcement.

Incorporated the Monk Fruit extract in the National Aministration of Medicines Food and Medical Technology, as a natural sweetener derived from a small Asian fruit, used internationally as an alternative to sugar (Joint Resolution No. 3/2026).

Released a series of regulatory, administrative, and operational measures that collectively reinforce SAT’s transition toward predictive tax supervision, digital interoperability, and enhanced compliance monitoring.

Approved a plan to shift from a sector-specific response to a broader inter-ministerial strategy to protect cocoa industry, which has been hit by falling international prices, weak local processing capacity, logistical bottlenecks and smuggling. The measures under consideration therefore extend beyond short-term support. They include tax incentives for exporters using official trade channels and repatriating export revenues to the DRC, continued distribution of improved seeds and fermentation equipment, and the construction of warehouses and storage facilities. The government also plans to organize smallholder farmers into cooperatives to strengthen their bargaining power and reduce dependence on intermediaries.
decision_making_institution: Government of Democratic Republic of the Congo

policydecision_details: On May 8, 2026 it was published the final rule that updates retailer stocking standards in the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP). This rule ensures that retailers carry a variety of foods that promote the health of SNAP participants. The rule also simplifies how foods are categorized, making the requirements easier for retailers to implement and FNS to oversee, strengthening the integrity of SNAP at all levels.
decision_making_institution: Government of United States of America

policydecision_details: The government of Bosnia and Herzegovina's Federation said it has adopted a decision to lend 20 million marka (USD 12 million) to local lender Union Banka, to launch a credit line for young people to address housing issues.

The World Bank Group has approved a new USD 1 billion financing package for Egypt aimed at supporting private sector-led growth, strengthening economic resilience, and advancing the country’s green transition.

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: Slovenia’s Parliament has adopted a law to gradually close the Velenje coal mine, the country’s last remaining mine, allocating EUR 1.13 billion (USD 1.31 billion) over the 2026 – 2045 period to support mine closure, land rehabilitation and a just transition for workers.
policycategory: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policydecision_details: Agreed to part of the demands made by the rural caucus and accepted the inclusion of some changes in the supplementary bill that cut fuel taxes in 2026. The proposal creates an exception to Brazil’s Fiscal Responsibility Law (LRF) by allowing revenue losses from fuel tax cuts to be offset through extraordinary federal revenue generated by oil price shocks, not through increases in other taxes, as current legislation requires. That includes additional royalty income, special participation payments, tax revenue from the oil and gas sector, proceeds from the sale of surplus pre-salt oil by PPSA and dividends paid to the federal government.

Agreed with Zambia on eliminated several trade barriers to facilitate easier movement of goods, services and people across their borders, making significant step toward enhancing bilateral trade relations and economic cooperation between the two neighbour countries.

policy_description: Subsidies on fuel, power and water
policydecision_details: Considered targeted cuts to fuel subsidies for higher‑income groups amid rising global prices, with potential implementation as early as next month.
policycategory: Subsidies on fuel, power and water

policydecision_details: Launched the National Social Policy (DSN) Action Plan 2026-2030, featuring 102 initiatives focused on prevention, empowerment, promotion and protection to strengthen social well-being and improve support for vulnerable groups nationwide.

Australia will introduce a domestic gas reservation scheme from 1 July 2027, requiring exporters to supply 20% of gas to the local market to lower prices and support industry. Australian federal government statement, 07/05/2026.

Cell‑cultured foods are made by growing animal or plant cells in controlled environments to create alternatives to products like meat. In Australia and New Zealand, they have been regulated since June 2025 under Food Standards Australia New Zealand (FSANZ) standards covering safety, production, and mandatory labelling, and only approved products can be sold as minced meat, steak or chicken fillets.

Allocated about 13 billion drams (approximately USD 34 million) for road improvements. The program, presented by the Prime Minister, covers 57.5 km of highways, including 0.9 km of interstate, 26.7 km of national, and 29.9 km of regional roads, along with three transport facilities.

Morocco has moved to tighten controls on exports of copper alloy ingots, requiring prior authorization for overseas shipments under new rules aimed at safeguarding domestic supply and curbing market distortions.

policy_description: Access to credit|Transport regulation and infrastructure
policydecision_details: Launched USD 224 million diaspora bond to fund infrastructure, called Patriotic Bond. The fund will support agroindustry, energy, housing and road projects. Government offers tax-free yields of up to 6.85 percent to attract investors.
policycategory: Access to credit|Transport regulation and infrastructure

policydecision_details: Moved to take full control of its main electricity provider and distributor, after the signature of decree approving its renationalisation. Energy of Cameroon (ENEO) is the backbone of the country’s electricity sector holding a monopoly over distribution, while operating dozens of power generation plants.

Sigend a decree authorizing the securing of two loans totaling CFA 7 billion from Deutsche Bank Spain. The financing will support the purchase of two fishing vessels and the redevelopment of facilities at the Youpwe fishing port in Douala. The first loan consists of a buyer’s credit worth CFA6.230 billion, while the second takes the form of a commercial loan of CFA787.796 million
Published an ordinance to formally establish the National Clinical Research Program, expected to reorganize and enhance clinical research in Brazil, making it more modern and nationally integrated.

policy_description: Other export restrictions|Fuel resources for production
policydecision_details: Extended fuel export restrictions to safeguard domestic supply, banning road exports of gasoline, diesel, jet fuel and other petroleum products, including to EAEU countries, from 21 May to 21 November 2026, with limited exemptions. Rail exports face tighter controls, while gasoline shipments remain allowed under approved plans. Additional restrictions on exports of light distillates and related products outside the EAEU will run from 1 July to 31 December 2026.
policycategory: Other export restrictions|Fuel resources for production

policy_description: Unspecified genetic resources and sanitary measures
policydecision_details: Significant changes are entering into force in Türkiye’s plant quarantine regime under the new Plant Quarantine Regulation dated 6 May 2026 as: • GMO controls have been expressly regulated for the first time, • the concept of “high-risk plants” has been introduced into the legislation, • all procedures have been transferred to a digital system (BKKTS), • certification and traceability obligations have been expanded, • transit, re-export and returned goods procedures have been substantially restructured, and • stricter enforcement measures have been introduced in relation to fraudulent certificates and non-compliant shipments.
policycategory: Unspecified genetic resources and sanitary measures

policydecision_details: Cabinet approves emergency credit line guarantee scheme 5.0 to support indian airlines.
The United Arab Emirates and Qatar have signed several agreements and memorandums of understanding in key sectors, including economy and development, according to a joint statement.
The United Arab Emirates and Qatar have signed several agreements and memorandums of understanding in key sectors, including economy and development, according to a joint statement.

Started distributing winter wheat inputs under the Presidential Input Programme (PIP). The commencement of input distribution comes as Government intensifies efforts to ensure farmers plant on time and meet this year’s winter wheat production targets. For the 460 irrigation schemes managed by the Agricultural and Rural Development Authority (ARDA), inputs are being supplied directly as complete packages to business units, bypassing traditional retail channels and minimising bureaucratic delays.

policy_description: Subsidies on fuel, power and water
policydecision_details: Introduced TZS 259 (USD 0.09) per litre diesel subsidy to protect consumers from escalating global oil prices.
policycategory: Subsidies on fuel, power and water

policy_description: Fisheries and aquaculture measures and regulations
policydecision_details: Algeria announced a plan to accelerate the development of its aquaculture sector and increase domestic fish supply. Ministry of Agriculture said the plan aims to double aquaculture production to 20,000 tons by 2026.
policycategory: Fisheries and aquaculture measures and regulations

policydecision_details: On 5 May 2026, a package of legislative changes was adopted in Sweden, aimed at strengthening competition in private and public markets. The package includes amendments to the Swedish Competition Act, the introduction of a new chapter establishing a new competition tool, and a new law on public sector sales activities, with most provisions entering into force on 1 August 2026.

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: Announced plans to expand electricity supply across the country and that the government would continue to invest heavily in both electricity and potable water infrastructure as part of efforts to drive socio-economic development and enhance the well-being of citizens.
policycategory: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policydecision_details: Secured voluntary MFN pricing agreements with 17 major pharmaceutical firms and aims to extend similar deals to most makers of sole-source brand-name drugs and biologics. It is also working with Congress to formalise these agreements into law to sustain patient access to lower prices.
decision_making_institution: Government of United States of America

policydecision_details: The Prime Minister’s Official Dispatch No. 38/CD-TTg (May 5, 2026) issued for strengthened measures to prevent and address IP infringements, aiming to raise enforcement standards.

Launched a strategic partnership with Africell to relaunch Sierratel as a Mobile Virtual Network Operator, marking a majort turning point in the county's telecommunication sector. Under the MVNO arrangement, Africell will provide network coverage, technical backbone, and sustained investment, while Sierratel will focus on customer service delivery, market engagement, and product innovation. The model allows for the immediate rollout of services without requiring heavy public sector capital expenditure.

Advanced a strategy to enhance the value chains of its special economic zones (SEZs). The government is accelerating SEZ development to attract investment in strategic sectors, including finance, high-quality tourism, and healthcare services.
Planned to phase out electricity imports from Russia by 2027, despite a projected short‑term deficit of 1–1.2 billion kWh this year to be covered by Russian supplies.

policy_description: Price intervention on cash crop commodities
policydecision_details: Expanded Minimum Support Price (MSP) measures, including procurement of over 9,000 tonnes of sunflower in Karnataka (worth ~₹69 crore, appx. US$8.3 million) and increasing gram procurement in Maharashtra to 800,000 tonnes (over ₹4,800 crore, appx. US$580 million), along with a 30‑day extension of the purchase period. These steps aim to ensure fair prices, strengthen farmer incomes, and reduce exposure to market volatility.
policycategory: Price intervention on cash crop commodities

policy_description: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
policydecision_details: Introduced new urban forestry and water management initiatives to address climate risks, highlighting intensifying heat as clear evidence of climate change, underscoring the urgency of adaptation efforts.
decision_making_institution: Government of Taiwan Province of China
policycategory: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures

policydecision_details: Announced delays in implementing food safety regulations were due to funding constraints. The 2024 Food Safety Act mandates that 14 supporting regulations be drafted and gazetted within three months.

The European Commission (EC) adopted the Middle East Crisis Temporary State Aid Framework (METSAF), as part of its “AccelerateEU” strategy to address rising energy costs and reduce Europe’s dependency on imported fossil fuels. The new framework aims to equip Member States with State aid tools to mitigate the impact of the de facto closure of the Strait of Hormuz and the resulting sharp increases in global prices for oil, gas and fertilisers.

A new legislation aiming to protect consumers from abusive practices in relation to loans of up to EUR 100 000 (USD 116 000) has been prepared by the Development Ministry. The legislation introduces a cap on the total repayment amount of consumer loans, limiting it to between 30%-50% above the amount borrowed-broadly in line with the European average.

Modified the regulatory framework for tobacco products, nicotine, and alternative consumption devices through a set of regulations covering foreign trade, health regulations, and administrative control. These measures are implemented through a decree from the National Executive Branch, a resolution from the Ministry of Health, and a provision from ANMAT (National Administration of Drugs, Food and Medical Technology), which together constitute different levels of decision-making within the Argentine legal system.

policy_description: Employment programmes|Agricultural expenditure in the national budget
policydecision_details: Approved a TZS 1.105 trillion (USD 409 million) for the Ministry of Agriculture for the 2026/27 financial year, paving the way for a nationwide rollout of the Bulding a Better Tomorrow programme. The initiative, targeting youth unemployment through commercial agriculture, is transitioning from pilot projects to full-scale implementation across councils and constituencies.
policycategory: Employment programmes|Agricultural expenditure in the national budget

policydecision_details: Promoted the formation of modern agricultural communities to shift from small-scale farming to more competitive, integrated agribusiness, supported by loans, a $35 million government credit package (2025–2027), and additional bank financing to boost productivity and scale. In addition, FTB Bank, Chip Mong Bank and Wing Bank have allocated around $25 million in financing for modern agricultural communities.
On May 4, Singapore and New Zealand signed the world’s first legally binding bilateral agreement to ensure that essential supplies will continue to flow smoothly, even in times of crisis.

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: Announced the authorisation for 5 000 MW of private renewable projects, bringing the total commitment for renewable capacity to 16 000 MW.
policycategory: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policydecision_details: Announced that the daily minimum wage would increase up to USD 7.63.
Planned to phase out the CESS para-tariff by 2029 under a structured reform outlining timelines and safeguards to replace the long-standing levy. CESS: Commodity Export Subsidy Scheme.
Revealed an initiative to develop a regulatory framework to establish a minimum wage in the country.

The Ministry of Labor, Family, Social Affairs and Equal Opportunities (MDDSZ) has officially extended the validity of the decree that allows for faster employment of foreigners. Originally set to expire on April 30, the accelerated procedures will now remain in effect until October 31, 2026.

policy_description: Fisheries and aquaculture measures and regulations|Ecosystem and habitat preservation
policydecision_details: Implemented the annual fishing ban in the Gulf of Nicoya. This restriction period is vital for rigeneration of marine species and the overall health of the ecosystem.
policycategory: Fisheries and aquaculture measures and regulations|Ecosystem and habitat preservation

policy_description: Nutrition and health policy|Food safety regulations and standards
policydecision_details: Conducted a training to strengthen early warning surveillance systems and promote safer tourism practices.
policycategory: Nutrition and health policy|Food safety regulations and standards

policydecision_details: Enacted the provision 1/2026 joining Brazil and Uruguay in adopting regulatory frameworks that allow the issuance of a declaration directly by the exporter, gradually replacing - as will be seen later - the traditional Certificate of Origin managed before an authorized entity.

Raised diesel, kerosene and jet A-1 prices for the second consecutive month. The Energy Regulation Board (ERB) increased diesel prices from approximately USD 1.10 to USD 1.26 per liter, kerosene from USD 1.19 to USD 1.30 per liter, and Jet A-1 aviation fuel from USD 1.29 to USD 1.41 per liter. Petrol prices remained unchanged at approximately USD 1.01 per liter, as wholesale price movements stayed within the ERB's pricing adjustment threshold.

Announced that new minimum wage will take effect from January 2027, noting that the decision has taken into account the country's economic conditions, rising costs of living and the government's committment to boosting workers motivtion to enhance efficiency in services delivery.

Launched a pilot program that will provide free, easy-to-use chlorine water treatment to households through maternal and child health services, with the support of J-PAL Africa. By using routine health visits, similar to how other preventive health products like bed nets are given for free, the program aims to make safe drinking water reliable and accessible for households with young children.

Granted a one-month tax exemption on LNG imports to help reduce electricity costs. The measure, covering customs duty, commercial tax, and advance income tax, aims to lower power generation expenses amid rising global fuel prices.
Extended a six‑month ban on exports of ferrous scrap, effective May 1, covering waste and scrap from ferrous and non‑ferrous metals, including copper, aluminum, and lead.

Revised Fisheries Law introducing stricter aquaculture standards, limiting fishing capacity, and prohibiting unregistered vessels from operating or accessing fuel, water, or ice. The law was adopted on 27 Dec 2025.

The Guide to Canada’s Export Control List issued in January 2026, comes into effect from 1 May 2026, identifies the items included on the export control. Categories distinguish between U.S.-focused quotas (CUSMA) and EU-focused rules (CETA). In the agriculture and foods session, changes relate to milk products, peanut butter, sugar-contanig products and processed foods.

Proposed updates to its list of aquatic species susceptible to key diseases, seeking stakeholder input as part of efforts to strengthen import controls and domestic disease management for aquatic animals, given the significant risks such diseases pose to wild and farmed populations. This consultation ran from March 2, 2026, to May 1, 2027.

Enforced new regulations governing small commerce and retail trade. The reform reaffirms that small commerce and retail trade are reserved for Congolese economic operators. It maintains the government's position of protecting local commercial activities for nationals.The regulations also introduce an important distinction. Certain capital-intensive specialized retail activities will remain open to foreign investors, under conditions set by the regulations. The stated objective is not to exclude foreign capital entirely, but to redirect it toward segments requiring more structured investment.

Implemented the new EU Guidelines on preferential origin relating to the Interim Trade Agreement between EU and Mercosur. The preferential origin system introduced by the Agreement is based on self-certification by the exporter, replacing the traditional certificates issued by public authorities. The preferential tariff treatment must be requested by the importer and demonstrated through origin documentation; the request may also be made within two years from the date of importation. For EU exporters, the REX system is central: except for shipments of a value lower than EUR 6,000, registration and inclusion of the REX number in the origin attestations is required. For Mercosur countries, a five-year transitional regime is provided, allowing the use of certificates of origin issued by public authorities as an alternative to self-certifications. Other key provisions worth highlighting are: a general tolerance rule of 10% of the ex-works value for the use of non-originating materials; bilateral cumulation, under which originating materials from the EU used in processing in Mercosur may be treated as originating materials of Mercosur and vice versa; and the possibility of duty drawback, i.e. the refund or suspension of duties on non-originating materials used in the production of goods exported under preference.
Belarus raised export duties on liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) to the Russian level from May 1, 2026, with the corresponding resolution signed by Belarusian Prime Minister.
Continued to progressively expand general licenses for the energy sector activties involving Venezuelan-origin oil, gas and petrochemical activities.
Implemented zero-tariff treatment for imports from al 53 African countries with which it has diplomatic relations.

Issued new blocking sanctions on Cuba to operate in or have operated in the energy, defense and related materiels, metals and minim, financial services or security sector of the Cuban economy; be owned, controlled, or directed by, or to have acted or purported to act for on oh behalf of, directly or indirectly, the Government of Cuba; own or control, directly or indirectly, any person whose property or interests in property; have materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services to or in support of, the Government of Cuba or any person whose property or interests in property are blocked under this EO; be or have been a leader, official, senior executive officer, or member of the board of directors of the Government of Cuba or an entity whose property or interests in property are blocked under this EO; be a political subdivision, agency, or instrumentality of the Government of Cuba; be responsible for or complicit in, or to have directly or indirectly engaged in or attempted to engage in, serious human rights abuse in Cuba;be responsible for or complicit in, or to have directly or indirectly engaged or attempted to engage in, corruption related to Cuba, including corruption by, on behalf of, or otherwise related to the Government of Cuba, or a current or former official at any level of the Government of Cuba, such as the misappropriation of public assets, expropriation of private assets for personal gain or political purposes, or bribery; orbe an adult family member of a person designated under this EO.
decision_making_institution: Government of United States of America

policydecision_details: Adopted a new law to reorganize the country's drinking water supply and sanitation sector. The reform is designed to improve access to clean water, strengthen hygiene systems, and attract private investment into a sector considered vital for public health and development.

Notified rice importers an updated framework that introduces an annual authorization process for customs clearence, tightening oversigth of the secto amid a broader push to strengthen domestic revenue collection and trade governance.
Outlined the 1 May Day worker protections, including a higher holiday bonus for gig workers (minimum 25% of average net income) and a nationwide minimum wage increase.

Accused China of circumventing import restrictions by routing vegetables through Vietnam and relabeling them as Vietnamese products. The claims come as Taiwan, Province of China maintains a ban on more than 1,000 Chinese agricultural and fishery items.
decision_making_institution: Government of Taiwan Province of China

policydecision_details: Signed a project with FAO funded by the Swiss Agency for Development and Cooperation (SDC) to establish a National Forest Monitoring and Assessment (NFMA) system. The project will introduce regular national forest inventories, combining field data with remote sensing and GIS to produce reliable information on forest cover, health, biodiversity, and carbon stocks.

Banned the import of goods made wholly or partly through forced labour under a new Commerce Ministry order. Importers will have to provide documentary proof that their products are free from forced labour.

Announced the mandatory ethanol blend in gasoline from 30 to 32 percent and increased the biodiesel mandate from 15 to 16 percent. This increase will require that more maize output will shift from feed industry to fuel industry.
The Korea Credit Guarantee Fund (KODIT) and Woori Bank signed an agreement enabling KODIT to provide KRW 222 billion (USD 150 million)in loan guarantees to support SMEs affected by the global crisis.

Announced minimum wage adjustments for the years 2026 and 2027. Adjustments vary from 60 percent to 70 percent and the wage difference for the months prior to the measure (from January to April 2026) must be compensated by companies by 31 July 2026.
Introduced a 18 percent VAT obligations on B2C sales for non-resident suppliers of digital services and online goods (Minsterial Order No 004/26/10/TC).

Established, with the Administrative Resolution No 0009/2026 of the National Health Authority of Nicaragua, the full digitalization of procedures for products intended for human consumption and definitively eliminating the use of paper in the registration and renewable processes for food and beverages. The new regulation requires that all applications be processed exclusively through the Karplus System. This platform now centralizes all procedures related to new sanitary registrations, renewals (with or without changes), and modifications.

The State Bank of Vietnam is drafting a new circular to revise foreign exchange management regulations for foreign direct investment into Vietnam, allowing earlier opening of investment accounts and improving flexibility in capital flow management. The draft circular is intended to replace Circular 06/2019/TT-NHNN.

Introduced hourly wage model and equal pay reforms as part of broader labour reforms. The minimum wage has risen to 345 manats (about USD 203), the average monthly salary to 1,099 manats (about USD 646), and the minimum pension to 320 manats (about USD 188).

Ruled out a 25% tax on existing gas export contracts, rejecting what was described as a “populist” proposal. Emphasizing that a global fuel crisis is the worst time to risk relations, the decision aims to protect partnerships with Asian trading partners, and the upcoming federal budget will not include such a tax.

Urged national consensus to shift from crisis response to long-term water security, including building large reservoirs and dams, stressing that Pakistan’s water challenges cannot be addressed in isolation.
The Central Bank of Uzbekistan has amended foreign exchange rules, allowing individuals to transfer funds for personal, non‑commercial purposes between any bank accounts.
Announced that USD 1 billion from the National Development Fund will be allocated to import basic goods such as sugar, rice, red meat and animal feed.

policy_description: Subsidies on fuel, power and water
policydecision_details: Decided to implement some cuts in public spending to make funds available to offer independent bus operators of the Belize Bus Association a USD 3.00 per gallon fuel subisidy.
policycategory: Subsidies on fuel, power and water

policydecision_details: Adopted the National Policy on Food and Nutrition 2026-2035 and directed the Federal Ministry of Budget and Economic Planning to present the policy to the Federal Executive Council for ratification.

policy_description: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
policydecision_details: Launched a public–private Voluntary Carbon Market Alliance, chaired by the Korea Chamber of Commerce and Industry, to serve as a governance platform linking supply and demand, addressing regulatory gaps, and supporting market activity.
policycategory: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures

policydecision_details: Reviewed a draft law since March 18, 2026 to amend the Customs Code, aiming to comprehensively regulate e‑commerce within national and EAEU customs frameworks by introducing new provisions to the existing legislation, the Code of Kazakhstan "On Customs Regulation in the Republic Of Kazakhstan".

FAO will deliver cash assistance directly to beneficiaries via bKash, improving transparency, security, and efficiency. Recipients can instantly access funds in their accounts and use them for everyday needs such as payments, transfers, and mobile services without visiting agents.

Planned to introduce a five-year income tax exemption for new immigrants and returning residents relocating in 2026, covering locally earned income such as salaries and self-employment earnings, as part of efforts to encourage aliyah.

The World Bank has endorsed USD 24.5mn in grant financing for the Technical Assistance for Sustainable Agricultural Transformation (TASAT) project in Philippines. The funding acts as a companion to a massive USD 1bn loan intended to pivot the country away from its rigid obsession with rice self-sufficiency.

policycategory: Anti-dumping duties, countervailing duties, safeguard measures

policydecision_details: Approved the Judges Salaries and Pensions Bill 2025 to fulfil a constitutional obligation and correct a gap in which judges, unlike magistrates, do not receive pension. The pension will be calculated solely on the basis of salary, not alowances.

Implemented the Occupational Safety and Health (OSH) Bill 2025, by issuing a Logitech webcam and USB hub adapter to each senator to promote uniformity, reliability and the overall quality of virtual sittings and to strengthen the official record of proceedings. The Act does not apply to any owner or occupier of a private residence, the surrounding land, or any associated property where a domestic worker provides domestic work.

The government plans to reform land administration by reclaiming unused and illegally occupied public land, introducing digital systems, streamlining registration processes, and strengthening oversight to improve transparency, reduce corruption, and protect agricultural land.

policy_description: Legal and regulatory measures for consumer protection
policydecision_details: Proposed new e‑commerce rules to strengthen consumer protection, addressing complaints on product quality, payments, and delivery. About 60% of cases were resolved in favor of consumers, with compensation totaling roughly 350 million soums (around USD 28,000).
policycategory: Legal and regulatory measures for consumer protection

policydecision_details: Launched the National Artificial Intelligence Strategy in Accra. The strategy addresses sectors including healthcare, agriculture, education, finance, and public service delivery, and covers measures including AI training for government ministers, the introduction of AI performance indicators across ministries, departments and agencies, and the deployment of AI by the Ghana Revenue Authority. The government states that the strategy aims to position Ghana as an AI hub in West Africa and to localise AI systems to reflect Ghanaian languages and cultural contexts. Implementation will be coordinated across government institutions including the National Information Technology Agency, Data Protection Commission, and Cyber Security Authority, with support from international partners including GIZ, UNDP, and UNESCO.
Introduced new import tariffs ranging from 5 percent to 35 percent on 185 HS codes, covering finished goods and industrial outputs.

Implemented new import licensing rules for rice effectively halting shipments to Cotonou port and triggering a price slide in Indian markets. Importers must hold a USD 1.7 million deposit in a Public Treasury account and commit to monthly volumes of 50 000-100 000 tonnes.

The Republic is buying additional liquefied natural gas (LNG) from other parts of the world as the conflict in the Middle East disrupts shipments of the commodity used to generate electricity in the country.

Increased the maximum retail price of petro to RWF 2 938 (USD 0.88) per litre, while capping diesel at RWF 2 205 (USD 1.51) per litre, with the government intervening to shild transport and logistics from sharper costs increases.

The government decided on Tuesday, April 14th, that a solidarity levy will be imposed on fuel retailers if their actual retail price exceeds the objectively calculated price by more than 3%. The final decision on the draft law prepared by the Ministry of Economics (EM) will be made by the Saeima.

policy_description: Public institution|Establishment or modification of food stock
policydecision_details: Gazzetted the Food Reserve Act 2026, to continue the existence of the Food Reserve Agency and re-define its functions; re constitute the Board of the Agency and re-define its functions, continue the existence of the National Strategic Food Reserve; ensure national food security by maintaining sufficient levels of designated agricultural commodities to respond and provide food relief during emergencies or market and economic shocks; provide for the power of the Minister to designate agricultural commodities that are essential for food security; provide for the purchase of designated agricultural commodities by the Agency for purposes of the National Strategic Food Reserve; provide mechanisms for collaboration and cooperation with relevant regulatory and advisory agencies to ensure exchange of agricultural marketing information and the stabilisation of agricultural markets; repeal and replace the Food Reserve Act, 2020; and provide for matters connected with, or incidental to, the foregoing.

This equipment includes soaking tanks with capacities ranging from 800 kg to one tonne, 120-kg parboiling machines fitted with stainless steel sieves and fuelled by improved stoves, as well as drying tarpaulins. policydecision_details: Introduced 100 percent discount on iFood Club monthly fee for teachers, a subscription model that gather advantages within the platform conditioning access to the automatic validation of the CNBD in the offical system of the federal government.

Enacted the revised Foreign Trade Law of the People’s Republic of China, adopted on December 27, 2025. The updated legislation marks a notable shift in China’s trade policy, moving beyond its previous emphasis on openness to international trade toward a framework that places greater weight on protecting the domestic economy. This change is reflected in Article 1 of the law, which explicitly highlights objectives such as safeguarding national sovereignty, security, and development interests.

Launched a new 2026-2027 investment strategy focused on infrastructure, energy, human capital and private sector competitiveness, to strengthen the impact of public investments. Flagship projects include the Tambacounda dry port, the Grand Water Transfer project, the Southern and Central agropoles, and the ports of Ndayane and Sendou. For the 2026 fiscal year, the government allocated CFA2 384.3 billion (USD 4 billion) to public investment.

Signed the Water Supply Project with EU. The Water Supply Project in the Greater Banjul Area (WASIB) will finance critical infrastructure to provide safely managed drinking water services in the Greater Banjul Area, The Gambia. WASIB addresses several challenges in the area, including ageing water supply facilities, high levels of non-revenue water, intermittent water supply, and depleting groundwater resources. policydecision_details: On March 20, 2024, the Ministry of Economy and Finance issued Prakas No.170 on Tax Incentives for the Agricultural Sector. This regulation aims to consolidate previous tax incentives into a single document and expands the scope of agricultural products eligible for these incentives. The tax incentives apply to the planting, producing, local supplying, and exporting of paddy rice, rice, corn, beans, peppers, cassava, cashew nuts, rubber, Pailin longans, mangos, bananas, as well as livestock farming, aquacultures, and local oil palm products used as raw materials for producing animal feed. Enterprises operating within the scope of this Prakas are eligible for a range of tax incentives, including: 1. Suspension of the monthly prepayment of income tax and the minimum tax until the end of 2025. 2. Exemption from the withholding obligation on payments for services performed by persons not under the self-assessment regime until the end of 2025. 3. The value-added tax will be borne by the State. To qualify for these tax incentives, enterprises in the agricultural sector must comply with key conditions outlined in this Prakas, such as keeping proper accounting records and filing tax returns correctly, among others. Non-compliance with these requirements could lead to the revocation of the tax incentives.

policy_description: Opinions of the General Office of the State Council on Adopting an All-Encompassing Approach to Food and Building a Diversified Food Supply System
policydecision_details: The Opinions of the General Office of the State Council on Adopting an All-Encompassing Approach to Food and Building a Diversified Food Supply System is a strategic guidance policy document proposed by the Chinese government to cope with future food security and sustainable development challenges and strengthen food supply security. The Opinions mainly focus on the big food view and aim to broaden food sources and build a diversified food supply system to ensure China's food security and nutritional needs. The core concept of the Big Food View is to break through the traditional thinking of single supply of grains such as rice, wheat, and corn, and extensively develop and utilize various food resources, including grains, grains, feed, vegetables, fruits, fish, livestock, bacteria, insects, and other resources, forming a diversified food supply system. This comprehensive and multi-channel food security concept not only focuses on the food on arable land, but also involves the development and utilization of non-traditional food resources such as aquatic products, agroforestry, forage, grassland resources, and microorganisms. Key points proposed in the document include: 1.Diversified Agricultural Production: Promoting other crops like beans, potatoes, and developing livestock, fishery, and modern agriculture technologies; 2. Technological Innovation: Encouraging innovations in agriculture (e.g., gene breeding, smart agriculture) to boost production efficiency; 3. Sustainable Resource Use: Enhancing land and water use efficiency through practices like water-saving agriculture; 4. Green and Circular Agriculture: Reducing the environmental impact by promoting sustainable and low-carbon farming; International Cooperation on Food Security: Strengthening global agricultural partnerships and improving food reserves; Healthy Diets: Promoting balanced nutrition and food safety for better public health.

policy_description: Strategy on Aquaculture, Rural Development and Fishery 2017-2027
policydecision_details: The Strategy on Agriculture, Rural Development and Fisheries is a national policy with a cross-sectoral approach. The timeframe of the policy is 7 years between 2021 and 2027. The purposes of this policy are (I) to ensure the sustainable development of the agri-food sector to meet the needs of people facing medium and long-term challenges related to food security, livelihoods, climate change, and biodiversity loss, and (II) to develop rural households and become more competitive in rural areas, based on policies that support sustainable use of natural resources, efficient use of agricultural and fishing inputs, and agricultural knowledge and innovation.
